questions.question: In while (input != -1) { process(input); input = readNext(); } what is the sentinel value and why while?
options: The sentinel is process() and while is used for a fixed number of items
The sentinel is -1 and while because the number of data items is unknown
The sentinel is 0 and while is used to iterate over an array
There is no sentinel; it is an infinite loop
explanations: process() is not a sentinel value; -1 is.
Correct. -1 marks the end of the data and while is appropriate because you do not know how many there will be.

questions.question: Why is do-while appropriate for validating user input?
options: It checks the condition before reading, avoiding reading invalid data
It guarantees the input is requested at least once before checking
It allows a fixed number of attempts without a counter
explanations: No: do-while checks AFTER, so the first read always happens.
Correct. The post-check guarantees that the body (requesting input) runs at least once.
The attempt limit requires a separate counter; do-while does not provide it.
Correct. It prints 0, then n becomes 1. The condition 1 <= 0 is false, so it ends.
It does not print 1 because after the increment the condition is already false.
